identity.description: Prototype-based partitioner; the clustering default. Alternates assign-to-nearest-centroid / recompute-centroid steps to minimize within-cluster squared Euclidean distance, yielding k compact spherical segments plus a readable k×p centroid matrix. k is selected by a silhouette sweep, not fixed a priori. Segmentation deliverable first, supervised feature second — see additionalObservations for the demand-gate lesson.

emits.note: hard assignment via nearest centroid; the fitted knowledge is the k×p cluster_centers_ matrix, exposed as params-as-output and readable per-feature like coefficients
transform() = distance-to-each-centroid matrix; a k-dimensional representation consumable as downstream features

portTypeProposals.name: centroids
portTypeProposals.why: a dedicated per-model centroid port would let profilers / nearest-centroid scorers consume the k×p matrix as typed data; today it rides as paramsAsOutput on the cluster-id emission, with 'coefficients' the nearest existing port if a typed edge is ever needed

n_clusters.note: selected by silhouette sweep over the range, not treated as a known constant

invariances.why: the objective sums per-feature SQUARED differences; a feature measured in larger units contributes quadratically more and single-handedly steers every centroid
Euclidean distances are not preserved under nonlinear monotone maps, so log/rank transforms change assignments and centroids
Euclidean distance is undefined when any coordinate is missing — imputation is a hard precondition
centroid updates take MEANS of coordinates; the mean of one-hot columns is not a category and Euclidean geometry on encodings distorts neighborhoods
minimizing within-cluster squared Euclidean distance implicitly assumes isotropic, similar-variance, similar-size clusters — elongated or varying-density structure gets sliced wrongly
Lloyd's step is O(n·k·p) per iteration and mini-batch variants extend it to millions of rows; the floor is only k << n
any new point — however far outside the training support — is confidently assigned to the nearest centroid with no notion of 'none of the above'

featureStats.why: the ratio of largest to smallest feature variance predicts how badly the squared-Euclidean objective is dominated by one feature — large spread makes the scale placement non-negotiable

measures cluster TENDENCY against a uniform-noise null; near 0.5 means any k-means partition is formatting noise, and even a high value only licenses segmentation, never supervised lift (see additionalObservations)
the smallest plausible cluster must still hold enough rows to estimate a stable centroid; tiny n/k invites empty-cluster reseeding and unstable partitions

modelMetrics.why: the family's honest fit measure — cohesion vs separation under the SAME distance the model optimizes; there is no holdout AUC for an unlabeled task
k is a hyperparameter, not a known — the silhouette sweep across k is how the partition count is chosen and defended
a partition that does not reproduce (adjusted Rand index) across resampled/reseeded fits is initialization noise, not structure — stability is the unsupervised analogue of a holdout
a near-empty cluster signals k set too high or scale problems; a single dominant cluster signals no real structure at this k

edgeCases.condition: empty cluster during a Lloyd iteration
edgeCases.behavior: sklearn relocates the centroid to the farthest point; the partition becomes reseed-sensitive and unstable across runs
the highest-variance feature dictates all assignments; other features are cosmetic
spherical bias slices true segments across boundaries
k-means still returns k confident segments — an artifact

driver.wrapperNeeds: none (fit/predict/transform native; predict assigns NEW points by nearest centroid, so score-path reuse works out of the box)
driver.threadSafety: fit is OpenMP-threaded; predict/transform are thread-safe

placementClaims.why: Euclidean distance is undefined on NaN — no assignment can be computed with missing coordinates
heavy-tailed features stretch Euclidean geometry; log/Yeo-Johnson makes clusters closer to the isotropic shape the objective assumes
scale-sensitive by mechanism — without standardization the objective is a single-feature contest, not a multivariate segmentation

categoricals must be numeric before distances exist at all; note one-hot inflates dimensionality and flattens Euclidean contrast — heavy-categorical inputs are a bank-entry toward mode-based alternatives

additionalObservations.note: Real-data validation lesson: cluster tendency (Hopkins) alone does NOT imply supervised lift. Segments that reproduce cleanly under bootstrap can still add zero AUC when appended as a feature to a downstream classifier. Clusters are a segmentation deliverable FIRST (profiling, targeting, reporting) and a candidate feature SECOND — gate cluster-feature promotion on measured lift in the supervised pipeline, never on cluster-quality metrics alone.
